statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits at the low-band floor because the entire assessed window falls inside the CME weekend halt and no Nasdaq-100 price path can form.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON with no danger window. Tail remains far below the block threshold for every hour published here. The risk described in this assessment is the magnitude of the repricing gap carried into the Sunday reopen at 22:00Z, which falls outside this window, rather than any path inside it.
headline: A 5% ten-year, $100 oil and a 14.81 VIX sit out the weekend halt after a record-scale expiry, with Tail pinned at its structural floor
body: The entire assessed window falls inside the CME weekend halt. Nasdaq-100 cash closed Friday at 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% against a 29,447.00 previous close, finishing near the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range. The E-mini NQ printed last at 29,917.25, up 0.59%, having ranged 29,648.00-29,993.25. VIX fell 4.08% to 14.81 and closed at the low of a 14.80-15.63 range. The tape was dispersed rather than directional: the S&P 500 rose 0.17% to 7,650.50 and the Nasdaq Composite 0.39% to 26,522.55 while the Dow slipped 0.18% to 51,682.64. The macro backdrop behind those marks is unusually tight. The FOMC raised the federal funds target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.00% on 16 September, its first increase since 2023, on a unanimous vote, with the median projection showing one further 25bp move by year-end. The 10-year Treasury closed at 4.998%, up 5.1 basis points, after an intraday 5.008% print that marked the highest levels since July 2007; the 2-year stood at 4.67% in the H.15 release for 17 September. WTI near $100.30 fell 1.58% and Brent near $103.87 fell 0.91%, a third consecutive decline, with Strait of Hormuz transit still running well below normal against a persistent Iran-related backdrop. Friday also cleared roughly $7 trillion of options notional in the second-largest triple witching on record, about a quarter of the market, with Citadel Securities noting that positioning which had dampened realized moves can change materially once it rolls off. That is a conditional sensitivity for the new week, not an observed condition. Tail is held at the low-band floor for every hour published here for a structural reason rather than a benign one: with no venue open, no price path can deny mean reversion, and none of the amplifiers that would justify a higher reading - shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, holding near session extremes - can form. The divergence between a 14.81 VIX and a 5% 10-year, $100 oil and a tightening Fed is a genuine latent fragility, but it is carried as unpriced weekend information that will express at the Sunday reopen at 22:00Z, roughly twenty hours after the final slot published here and outside this window.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail held a 5-19 band and Stress ran between 24 and 51, peaking near 51 through the European morning and the U.S. afternoon before falling away to 33, 28, 27, 26, 25 and 24 across the final six hours as cash trading ended and the contract settled. Confidence sat between 82 and 88 throughout. Dominant mode rotated from normal across the Asian and early European hours to trend-up into the U.S. pre-open, to mixed through the cash session, briefly back to trend-up into the close, and then to normal once the weekend halt began. No hour in the window reached the watch threshold.
outlookSummary: Every one of the 24 published slots falls inside the weekend halt: cash closed at 20:00Z, the E-mini printed last near 21:00Z, and futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, roughly twenty hours after the final slot here. Tail is held between 4 and 7 across the whole window, with a gradual lift through Saturday evening that reflects the growing stock of unpriced weekend information rather than any observed structure. Stress eases from 23 to a trough of 20 across the middle of Saturday and rebuilds to 27 by the final slot as the new week's setup comes into view. Confidence decays from 83 to 76 with distance from the verified evidence cutoff. Dominant mode is normal throughout, since no directional structure can form while the contract is closed. The named forward sensitivities - a post-expiry positioning reset, a 5% 10-year, $100 oil and a Fed that has resumed tightening - are conditional next-week inputs, and each would require observed price-path evidence after the reopen before it could lift Tail.
